steps.content: Only moments before, the farland representatives and Fraser guards had been locked in brutal combat. Now, they lie scattered across the floor, weapons slipping from slack fingers to clatter against the ground. Conscious but paralyzed, they stare up in pure terror at the one figure still standing among them.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Oh dear... I let my true nature slip and lost my temper. That's hardly becoming.
At that moment, Marcus lets out a low, hoarse laugh. He leans heavily against the splintered podium, face bloodless, and raises his head in one final, cold act of defiance.

steps.speaker: Marcus
steps.content: Heh... You think you've won? How arrogant... This is the farlands. No one will believe you. No one trusts a Disian...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Sigh, you're right, of course. My smile strategy won't be nearly as effective now. Once a peace envoy shows her fangs, trust becomes difficult to regain.
Margaret's gaze moves across the fallen—their expressions a mix of anguish and hate—before stopping on Saina. Even on one knee, braced by her sword, Saina's eyes meet hers, defiant and unbroken.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: And yet, all I ever wanted was to help everyone find peaceful solutions.

steps.speaker: Saina
steps.content: What could a Disian like you possibly understand...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Yes... a Disian speaking of the farlands' suffering is indeed laughable. But if you refuse even the person willing to listen and help... what change can you truly expect?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Tell me, will endless fighting, quarreling, killing... will any of that end your pain? Bring the happiness you seek?
Saina doesn't answer, instead turning her head away with bitter resentment.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: My words mean nothing to you, I understand. So...
She lifts her head. Her gaze sweeps over the shattered battlefield, past faces etched with hatred, greed, or confusion, then down the long corridor toward the palace entrance.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: ...My little bird should be returning any moment now.
With an elegant gesture, she beckons a snow-white dove in through the window. It alights on her fingers, nuzzles her temple, then bursts into flight, a streak of light arcing across the sky.
All eyes are irresistibly drawn to the white silhouette. It glides over the chaotic palace, down the long corridor, and lands, silent and certain, upon the shoulder of a young girl in the distance.
